item.title: Architecture & Data Contract
item.description:
The architecture is divided into a Data Lake path and a Serving path. The bridge between them is Lambda QMJ Loader: S3 creates new Parquet files, S3 sends an ObjectCreated event, and Lambda reads the file and writes items to DynamoDB.

Data Flow

Data Lake path
Sources → Backfill/Daily Ingestion → S3 Raw → Glue PySpark QMJ → S3 Processed

Serving path
S3 Processed -- ObjectCreated (*.parquet) --> Lambda QMJ Loader --> DynamoDB
DynamoDB --> Lambda Reader --> API Gateway --> Browser

Automation path
EventBridge Scheduler - - -→ Glue Python Shell Daily Ingestion

Data Contract

Dataset Grain Output location Consumer
us_prices_raw.parquet ticker + price_date raw_us_market/YYYY/MM/DD/ Glue PySpark QMJ
us_company_info.parquet ticker + snapshot_date raw_us_market/YYYY/MM/DD/ Glue PySpark QMJ
us_financials_raw.parquet ticker + report_date + period_type + snapshot_date raw_us_market/YYYY/MM/DD/ Glue PySpark QMJ
QMJ output Parquet One row per ticker at AS_OF_DATE processed_qmj/as_of_date=.../ Lambda QMJ Loader
DynamoDB item ticker + snapshot_date Table qmj_screener Lambda Reader

Architectural Principle – Event-Driven Serving. qmj_transform.py does not have PutItem or BatchWriteItem. The transform completes at S3 Processed; Lambda Loader is responsible for loading DynamoDB after detecting new Parquet files.

item.title: Create Glue PySpark Job for QMJ Transformation
item.description:
The QMJ Transform is a Spark ETL Job that reads all Raw Parquet files using recursiveFileLookup and outputs data partitioned by as_of_date.

Upload Transform Script

Step Action Technical Details
1 Amazon S3 → stock-screener-raw-your-name/glue-scripts/ Use the existing script S3 prefix
2 Select Upload Upload qmj_transform.py
3 Verify S3 URI s3://stock-screener-raw-your-name/glue-scripts/qmj_transform.py

Create Spark Job

Step Action Technical Details
1 AWS Glue → ETL jobs → Create job Open the Job creation wizard
2 Select job type Select Spark
3 Enter Job name us-stock-qmj-transform
4 Select IAM Role AWSGlueServiceRole-StockScreener
5 Select Script path URI of qmj_transform.py
6 Select Glue runtime Use the Spark runtime tested with your project
7 Select capacity Start small, increase after reviewing duration and memory
8 Open Job parameters Enter args in the table below
9 Select Save Save the job
10 Select Run Test with an AS_OF_DATE that has Raw data

Job Parameters

Key Sample value Source used
--RAW_BUCKET stock-screener-raw-your-name Override Raw Bucket
--RAW_PREFIX raw_us_market Override Raw prefix
--PROCESSED_BUCKET stock-screener-processed-your-name Override Processed Bucket
--PROCESSED_PREFIX processed_qmj Override Processed prefix
--AS_OF_DATE 2026-07-03 Cut-off date for info, prices, and financial reports
--LOOKBACK_DAYS 800 Lookback calendar days for price history
--MIN_PRICE_OBSERVATIONS 200 Parsed but not yet used as a filter in the current source 
In the Glue Console, keys must start with two dashes.
Example: --AS_OF_DATE

item.title: Run Local Price History Backfill
item.description:
The local backfill script ingests historical price data from 2023-01-01 to the current date. The code filters S&P 500 by MIN_MARKET_CAP = 10_000_000_000, partitions prices by individual trading date, and writes a company info snapshot on the day the script runs.

The local backfill script does not write us_financials_raw.parquet. Financials are ingested via the daily ingestion pipeline; the transformation code includes appropriate fallback handlers.

Install Local Dependencies

# Create a dedicated virtual environment for local backfill.
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Install packages required by source imports.
pip install boto3 pandas requests yfinance pyarrow tqdm lxml

Preparation and Run Backfill

Step Action Technical Details

2 Verify BUCKET_NAME Must be stock-screener-raw-your-name
3 Set MAX_TICKERS_FOR_TEST Test with a small batch first; use None when running full execution
4 Keep credentials outside source code boto3 uses the AWS CLI profile/credential chain
5 Run Python script Script calls STS to verify identity before crawling

item.title: Amazon Personalize and Result Analysis
item.description:
This article guides you on how to set up the AutoML cycle, create an API gateway to serve prediction results, and implement an optimal FinOps strategy for infrastructure costs.

Step 1: Initialize Dataset Group and Import data from S3

We need to load the processed CSV file from the personalize_data/ folder on S3 into the Machine Learning environment.

Step Action Technical details
1 Access service In the AWS Console search bar, type Personalize and select this service.
2 Create Dataset Group Click the Create dataset group button, name it news_recommender_group.
3 Select Domain Select the Domain type as Custom to optimize system customizability.
4 Define Schema Declare the mandatory interaction table structure including 3 core fields fully capitalized: USER_ID (string), ITEM_ID (string), TIMESTAMP (long/bigint).
5 Create Import Job In the Dataset import job section, name the job and point the S3 URL path accurately to the ETL-processed CSV file in Chapter 3.
6 Complete Grant S3 read permissions for Personalize via the automatic IAM Role creation option and click Start import. The data loading process takes about 10-15 minutes.

Step 2: Train artificial intelligence model (Training Solution)

Step Action Technical details
1 Initialize Solution In the Dataset Group menu, select the Solutions section -> Click Create solution.
2 Name the brain Enter the Solution name as news_behavior_matrix_model.
3 Select Algorithm In the Solution type section, select the specialized Recipe: aws-user-personalization.
4 Configure parameters Keep all Hyperparameters at AWS AutoML default levels.
5 Proceed to Train Click the Create and train solution button. AWS will automatically run algorithms to optimize the interaction matrix. This process takes about 40-50 minutes.

Step 3: Configure API Endpoint and FinOps “Hit and Run” Discipline

In order to send queries to get recommendation results from the application or source code, we need to provision a Campaign gateway connecting directly to the AI brain.

item.description:
Please perform the cleanup in the exact order of the tables below. Absolutely do not delete the S3 Data Lake before deleting other services, as it will cause a system bottleneck error.

1. Delete Machine Learning Layer (Highest priority)

This is the fastest “money burning” component. You must clean it up first.

4 Delete Dataset Group Finally, select Dataset groups -> Select the news_recommender_group group and click Delete.

item.title: Analyze & Implement QMJ PySpark Transformation
item.description:
The current transformation logic reads S3 Raw data and writes S3 Processed data without writing directly to DynamoDB; Chapter 4 handles DynamoDB publishing via Lambda triggers.

Seven Stages in Source Logs

Stage Log Actual Logic
1 Processing Company Info Select the most recent valid company info snapshot on or before AS_OF_DATE
2 Processing Prices Dedupe price, daily return, annualized volatility, 12-month momentum
3 Processing Financials Deduplicate financial reports, compute annualized ROE, debt-to-equity, and growth with fallback handlers
4 Merging data Join info, price metrics, and financial metrics by ticker
5 Calculating Percentiles Percentile 0–100, safety score, and QMJ score
6 Building Final Table Rank in descending order by qmj_score
7 Writing Processed Parquet Snappy Parquet by as_of_date

Formulas in Source Code

profitability_raw = financial_roe_raw
                    or return_on_equity from company info

growth_raw = financial_growth_raw
             or earnings_growth
             or revenue_growth

qmj_safety = average(safety_volatility_score, safety_debt_score)
qmj_score  = average(qmj_profitability, qmj_growth, qmj_safety)

value_recent_score and momentum_recent_score are computed and exported, but do not participate in the current qmj_score formula.

item.title: Create Lambda QMJ Loader with S3 Trigger
item.description:
qmj_transform.py outputs Parquet files to processed_qmj/as_of_date=YYYY-MM-DD/. This section configures Lambda QMJ Loader to ingest newly processed files.

This Lambda function operates in two modes:

Mode Invocation Method Purpose
s3_trigger S3 automatically sends event notifications when new .parquet files arrive Ingests new incremental output from Glue PySpark
backfill Lambda Test Event or Invoke API Scans the entire processed_qmj/ directory and loads historical QMJ scores

Architectural Principle – Source Boundary. This is not a Glue Publisher Job. S3 is the event source, Lambda is the compute layer that loads the Serving Store, and DynamoDB is the read-optimized projection for the website.

item.title: Deploy Daily Ingestion via Glue Python Shell
item.description:
Daily Ingestion fetches the S&P 500 ticker list from Wikipedia, pulls market data from Yahoo Finance via yfinance, and writes three Raw datasets.

us_prices_raw.parquet
us_company_info.parquet
us_financials_raw.parquet

Unlike local backfill execution, this step creates an AWS Glue Python Shell Job and pastes source code directly into the Glue Script editor.

Prerequisites Before Job Creation

Step Action Technical Details
1 Verify Raw Bucket The active S3 bucket is stock-screener-raw-khanh
2 Verify IAM Role Role AWSGlueServiceRole-StockScreener must have write permissions to raw_us_market/*
3 Verify Internet access The Job must be able to call Wikipedia, Yahoo Finance, and PyPI to install additional packages
4 Prepare source code Copy the complete daily_ingestion.py code at the bottom of this page
5 Do not hardcode credentials boto3.client("s3") automatically uses temporary credentials supplied by the Glue Role

Architectural Principle – Direct Editor. Glue Studio allows creating a new Python Shell script and writing code directly in the Script editor. You do not need to manually upload the script file to S3. AWS Glue still manages the Script Location for the Job at the service layer, but no manual operations with a glue-scripts/ directory are required.

item.title: Update IAM Role for AWS Glue
item.description:
In Chapter 2, the AWS Glue IAM Role was only granted permissions to work with S3. Now, because the Glue Job needs to write data directly to DynamoDB, you need to grant it these additional permissions.

Step Action Technical Details

item.title: Write IoT Simulator Source Code
item.description:
Create the simulator source code file

We will create a Python file that acts as a smart sensor on the truck. [cite_start]This file is responsible for simulating the journey data of 10 trucks and sending it to the AWS Cloud via the MQTT protocol. [cite: 1]

  1. Open the VS Code editor.
  2. Create a new file named truck_simulator.py.
  3. Copy and paste the code below into the file:
import time
import json
import random
from AWSIoTPythonSDK.MQTTLib import AWSIoTMQTTClient

# ==========================================
# 🔴 PARAMETER CONFIGURATION (WILL BE UPDATED IN CHAPTER 2)
# ==========================================
# This Endpoint will be obtained from AWS IoT Core Settings
IOT_ENDPOINT = "YOUR_AWS_IOT_ENDPOINT" 

# Path to security certificates
PATH_TO_ROOT_CA = "certs/AmazonRootCA1.pem"
PATH_TO_CERT = "certs/your-certificate.pem.crt"
PATH_TO_PRIVATE_KEY = "certs/your-private.pem.key"

CLIENT_ID = "Vaccine_Fleet_Simulator"
TOPIC = "telemetry/trucks"

# Create a simulated list of 10 trucks with origin coordinates
TRUCKS = [{"id": f"T-{100+i}", "lat": 10.7626 + (i * 0.01), "lon": 106.6602 - (i * 0.01)} for i in range(10)]

# ==========================================
# INITIALIZE SECURE MQTT CONNECTION
# ==========================================
myMQTTClient = AWSIoTMQTTClient(CLIENT_ID)
myMQTTClient.configureEndpoint(IOT_ENDPOINT, 8883)
myMQTTClient.configureCredentials(PATH_TO_ROOT_CA, PATH_TO_PRIVATE_KEY, PATH_TO_CERT)

print(f"Connecting to AWS IoT Core...")

# ==========================================
# DATA SENDING LOOP (1 SECOND/TIME)
# ==========================================
try:
    myMQTTClient.connect()
    print("✅ Connection successful!\n")
    while True:
        for truck in TRUCKS:
            # Generate random data for temperature and position
            data = {
                "truck_id": truck["id"],
                "temperature": round(random.uniform(2.0, 8.0), 2),
                "latitude": round(truck["lat"] + random.uniform(-0.001, 0.001), 6),
                "longitude": round(truck["lon"] + random.uniform(-0.001, 0.001), 6),
                "timestamp_ms": int(time.time() * 1000)
            }
            
            payload = json.dumps(data)
            myMQTTClient.publish(TOPIC, payload, 1)
            print(f"[{truck['id']}] Sent: {payload}")
            
        time.sleep(1) 

except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print("\n🛑 Stopped sending data.")
    myMQTTClient.disconnect()
  1. Save the file to your project directory.

Note: You need to replace YOUR_AWS_IOT_ENDPOINT and the certificate file names with the real information that you will initialize in the next System Deployment section.

Lambda source code

import json
import os
from decimal import Decimal

import boto3
from boto3.dynamodb.conditions import Key

TABLE_NAME = os.environ["DYNAMODB_TABLE"]
table = boto3.resource("dynamodb").Table(TABLE_NAME)


def json_default(value):
    # DynamoDB returns Decimal; API response requires JSON number.
    if isinstance(value, Decimal):
        return float(value)
    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported type: {type(value)}")


def response(status_code, body):
    return {
        "statusCode": status_code,
        "headers": {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
            "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET,OPTIONS",
            "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "Content-Type"
        },
        "body": json.dumps(body, default=json_default)
    }


def lambda_handler(event, context):
    params = event.get("queryStringParameters") or {}
    ticker = (params.get("ticker") or "").strip().upper()

    if not ticker:
        return response(400, {"message": "ticker is required"})

    result = table.query(
        KeyConditionExpression=Key("ticker").eq(ticker),
        ScanIndexForward=True
    )

    return response(200, {
        "ticker": ticker,
        "items": result.get("Items", [])
    })

<script>
    // ==========================================
    // ⚠️ PASTE YOUR API GATEWAY URL HERE
    // ==========================================
    const API_URL = "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx";
    
    let allData = []; // Store all historical data
    let dataTableInstance = null;

    function getScoreColorClass(score) {
        if (score === null || score === undefined) return "text-secondary";
        if (score >= 80) return "score-excellent";
        if (score >= 60) return "score-good";
        if (score >= 40) return "score-average";
        return "score-bad";
    }

    function formatNumber(num) {
        if (!num) return "-";
        return Number(num).toLocaleString('en-US', { maximumFractionDigits: 1 });
    }

    async function initApp() {
        try {
            const response = await fetch(API_URL);
            allData = await response.json();
            
            // Filter valid data
            allData = allData.filter(s => s.ticker != null);
            
            // 1. Extract unique dates/quarters (deduplicated and sorted newest first)
            const uniqueDates = [...new Set(allData.map(item => item.snapshot_date))].filter(Boolean).sort().reverse();
            
            // 2. Populate the date dropdown
            const dateSelector = document.getElementById("dateSelector");
            dateSelector.innerHTML = ""; // Clear "Loading..." text
            
            if(uniqueDates.length > 0) {
                uniqueDates.forEach(date => {
                    let option = document.createElement("option");
                    option.value = date;
                    option.innerText = date;
                    dateSelector.appendChild(option);
                });

                // Listen for date selection changes
                dateSelector.addEventListener("change", function(e) {
                    renderTableForDate(e.target.value);
                });

                // Automatically display data for the most recent date
                renderTableForDate(uniqueDates[0]);
            } else {
                dateSelector.innerHTML = "<option>No data available</option>";
            }
            
            // Hide loading screen
            document.getElementById("loading-screen").style.display = "none";

        } catch (error) {
            document.getElementById("loading-screen").innerHTML = `
                <h3 class="text-danger"><i class="fa-solid fa-triangle-exclamation"></i> API connection error</h3>
                <p class="text-secondary">${error.message}</p>
            `;
        }
    }

    // Filter and re-render table based on selected date
    function renderTableForDate(selectedDate) {
        // Filter data for the selected date
        let filteredData = allData.filter(item => item.snapshot_date === selectedDate);
        
        // Sort by Rank
        filteredData.sort((a, b) => (a.qmj_rank || 999) - (b.qmj_rank || 999));

        // Destroy old table before rendering the new one (prevents DataTables errors)
        if (dataTableInstance !== null) {
            dataTableInstance.destroy();
        }

        const tbody = document.querySelector("#stockTable tbody");
        tbody.innerHTML = ""; // Clear old data
        
        filteredData.forEach(stock => {
            const tr = document.createElement("tr");

            tr.innerHTML = `
                <td class="text-center text-secondary fw-bold">${stock.qmj_rank || '-'}</td>
                <td><span class="ticker-badge">${stock.ticker}</span></td>
                <td class="text-secondary small fw-bold">${stock.exchange || '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-truncate" style="max-width: 180px;" title="${stock.company_name || '-'}">${stock.company_name || '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-truncate" style="max-width: 150px;">${stock.industry_group || '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-truncate text-secondary" style="max-width: 150px;">${stock.sector_detail || '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-end fw-semibold">${formatNumber(stock.current_market_cap)}</td>
                <td class="text-end text-muted small">${formatNumber(stock.quarter_market_cap)}</td>
                
                <td class="text-center fs-6 border-start border-secondary ${getScoreColorClass(stock.qmj_score)}">${stock.qmj_score ? Number(stock.qmj_score).toFixed(1) : '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-center ${getScoreColorClass(stock.qmj_profitability)}">${stock.qmj_profitability ? Number(stock.qmj_profitability).toFixed(1) : '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-center ${getScoreColorClass(stock.qmj_growth)}">${stock.qmj_growth ? Number(stock.qmj_growth).toFixed(1) : '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-center ${getScoreColorClass(stock.qmj_safety)}">${stock.qmj_safety ? Number(stock.qmj_safety).toFixed(1) : '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-center ${getScoreColorClass(stock.value_recent_score)}">${stock.value_recent_score ? Number(stock.value_recent_score).toFixed(1) : '-'}</td>
                <td class="text-center ${getScoreColorClass(stock.momentum_recent_score)}">${stock.momentum_recent_score ? Number(stock.momentum_recent_score).toFixed(1) : '-'}</td>
            `;
            tbody.appendChild(tr);
        });

        // Re-initialize DataTables
        dataTableInstance = $('#stockTable').DataTable({
            pageLength: 20,
            lengthMenu: [20, 50, 100, 500],
            scrollX: true, 
            language: {
                search: "🔍 Filter stocks:",
                lengthMenu: "Show _MENU_ tickers",
                info: "Showing _START_ to _END_ of _TOTAL_ tickers",
                paginate: { next: "Next", previous: "Previous" },
                zeroRecords: "No matching tickers found."
            },
            order: [[0, 'asc']], 
            columnDefs: [
                { orderable: false, targets: [3, 4, 5] } 
            ]
        });
    }

    window.onload = initApp;
